coverage_note: Utah has no general public-sector collective bargaining statute in the sources captured. The Utah Fire Fighters' Negotiations Act (Utah Code 34-20a) is codified but was reported held invalid in Salt Lake City v. International Association of Firefighters, 563 P.2d 786 (Utah 1977); that opinion was not captured, so the cells that would rest on the Act are null. The Right to Work Law, which expressly reaches public employers, is recorded. Local bargaining or meet-and-confer arrangements adopted by individual employers are not covered.

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. The Right to Work Law covers the state and its political subdivisions and bars any employer from requiring dues or fees as a condition of employment; Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: No employer shall require any person to pay any dues, fees, or other charges of any kind to any labor union, labor organization or any other type of association as a condition of employment or continuation of employment.
